tagline.text: A Bicol city of faith, home to Our Lady of Peñafrancia and kinalas

items.credit: Ralff Nestor Nacor / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: Bicol's religious and educational hub, founded as Nueva Cáceres by the Spanish in 1575. Visit the Our Lady of Peñafrancia pilgrimage site and the old cathedral, taste Naga's signature noodle dish kinalas, then head out to the waterfalls on Mount Isarog and a wakeboard park.

Naga sits in the middle of Camarines Sur province in southeastern Luzon, on a plain where the Naga River, flowing down from Mount Isarog, meets the Bicol River. Its population of around 210,000 is similar to Legazpi's, but with its concentration of universities, churches, and commerce, it's nicknamed the "Heart of Bicol" and the "Queen City of Bicol." The name Naga is said to come from the narra (naga) trees once abundant in the area.
Spanish captain Pedro de Chaves founded "Nueva Cáceres" here in
, making it one of the oldest royal cities in the Spanish Philippines after Manila and Cebu. The founding of the Diocese of Nueva Cáceres in
made it the center of Catholicism in southern Luzon, and today's Naga Cathedral was begun in
and completed in
. With universities and seminaries clustered here, the streets are still full of students in uniform today.
What defines Naga most is devotion to Our Lady of Peñafrancia. It began when a Dominican priest built a stone shrine to house her image around
, and this devotion, now more than three centuries old, has grown into one of the largest Marian festivals in the Philippines. Every
September
, hundreds of thousands of pilgrims from across Bicol and abroad arrive, turning the whole city into a festival ground.

It isn't a city packed with tourist sights, but it's a good place to feel Bicolano faith and daily life by walking its churches and plazas, and to enjoy cheap, tasty local food. It also makes a convenient midway base for a Bicol trip that continues on to Caramoan island hopping, Calaguas Island, or Legazpi and Mount Mayon.
A modern basilica completed in
that houses the original image of Our Lady of Peñafrancia. It was designated a minor basilica in
. With its spacious gardens and tall bell tower, pilgrims come here constantly — if you visit during Mass, observe quietly from the back.
Completed in

, this Romanesque Revival cathedral was built low and thick-walled to withstand earthquakes. At the entrance to the plaza in front, the arch-shaped monument Porta Mariae has become one of Naga's signature photo spots.

This small stone chapel first housed the Marian image in the early 18th century and is also where the festival procession departs from. Visiting it alongside the basilica gives you a sense of the three centuries of devotion behind it.
Naga's signature noodle dish: chewy rice noodles in a rich broth made by slow-boiling beef or pork head meat, topped with a thick brown sauce, scallions, and a boiled egg. A bowl costs about
, and kinalas shops all over town serve it for breakfast or as a snack.

blocks.title: Strolling the Naga Riverside and Downtown Plazas

children.text: The old town around Plaza Quezon and Plaza Rizal, packed with shops, restaurants, and old buildings, is great for walking. The developed riverside along the Naga River also serves as the route for the festival's river procession.

blocks.title: Malabsay Falls and Panicuason Hot Springs

children.text: This waterfall on the slopes of Mount Isarog is about
40 minutes–1 hour
from downtown by car; walk down a forest stairway to a cool swimming hole. Nearby hot spring resorts in the Panicuason area offer pools ranging from cold to warm.

The Camarines Sur Watersports Complex (CWC), in Pili near the airport, is known for its cable-pulled wakeboard park. Beginner lessons are available, so first-timers can give it a try too. Check operating hours and rates before you go.
Starting as a small burger stand in Naga in
, this local chain has since spread across Bicol. It's a nostalgic favorite among locals, serving burgers, Filipino set meals, and Bicol Express at affordable prices.

Breakfast at a downtown kinalas shop
Explore Naga Cathedral, Porta Mariae, and the cathedral plaza
Walk to the Old Peñafrancia Shrine and stroll Plaza Quezon and Plaza Rizal
Lunch on Bicol Express and laing
Visit Peñafrancia Basilica and walk its gardens
Check into your hotel and rest
Walk the Naga riverside and take in the city at dusk
Dinner at Bigg's Diner or a local restaurant

items.title: Day 2
items.subtitle: The Slopes of Mount Isarog and Wakeboarding

children.text: After breakfast, head toward Panicuason by jeepney or chartered vehicle
Swim at Malabsay Falls and walk the forest trail
Relax and have lunch at a Panicuason hot spring resort
Return downtown and shop for pili nut and other souvenirs
Try wakeboarding at CWC, or relax at a cafe
Head to Naga Airport or the terminal and continue on to your next destination (Caramoan, Legazpi) or back to Manila
If you visit during the Peñafrancia Festival (September), adjust Day 2 around the festival schedule, and stake out a good spot early for the Traslación or the river procession.
Naga-bound buses from several companies, including DLTB, Peñafrancia, and Isarog, run daily from PITX, Cubao, and Pasay in Manila. The road distance is about
390km
, it takes about
8–10 hours
, and the fare is about
depending on class.
Most buses arrive at
Bicol Central Terminal
, which operates 24 hours. Taking an overnight bus gets you there early in the morning with a full day ahead of you.
Since
March 29, 2026
there have been no direct Manila–Naga flights. Cebgo, part of the Cebu Pacific group, flies to Naga Airport (WNP) in Pili from Clark, taking about
1 hour 20 minutes
, and the one-way fare is about
depending on the period. Flights are few and sell out early, so check the latest schedule.
The airport is about
15km
from downtown — around
30 minutes
by jeepney or van, or you can charter a taxi or tricycle. If no flight matches your schedule, you can also fly into Bicol International Airport (DRP) near Legazpi and take a van for about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
UV Express vans run frequently between Legazpi and Naga, taking about
2 hours–2 hours 30 minutes
for around
. Vans to Daet (for Calaguas) and Sabang Port (for Caramoan) also depart from the van terminal in downtown Naga.
The usual way to reach Malabsay Falls is to take a Panicuason-bound jeepney from downtown (about
), then transfer to a tricycle or motorcycle taxi.
The Philippine National Railways (PNR) Bicol Commuter train runs several times a day from Naga station to Sipocot, taking about
45 minutes
. The fare is cheap, so it's worth riding as a short train-trip experience.
The Naga–Legazpi section stopped running when Typhoon Uwan (Fung-wong) in
November 2025
destroyed a railway bridge in Guinobatan, Albay, and it had not reopened even as of
July 2026
. Use a van or bus to Legazpi, and check PNR notices for whether service has resumed.
Downtown is compact enough to explore on foot. For the basilica or malls a bit farther out, take a tricycle (about
) or jeepney.
To combine Malabsay Falls and CWC in a single day, a half-day to full-day tricycle or vehicle charter (about
) is convenient. Settle the route and waiting time before you set off.
Naga is in the Bicol region, exposed to the Pacific, so it rains fairly often year-round, with
February–May
being the relatively dry stretch. Waterfalls and mountain trails are less slippery and travel is pleasant during this period, but midday temperatures in
April–May
climb to around
, making it quite hot.
August–November
is when typhoons frequently cross the Bicol Peninsula, so keep flight cancellations and flooding in mind.
November–January
brings many cloudy, rainy days from the northeast monsoon.
The biggest event is the Peñafrancia Festival in
September
. On the
second Friday of September

, the Traslación procession sees barefoot male devotees called "Voyadores" carry the Marian image and the Divino Rostro (Holy Face) from the basilica to the cathedral; on the Saturday before the feast day, marking the end of a nine-day novena, the images are placed back on a boat for a river procession along the Naga River back to the basilica. Rooms book out months in advance during this period, so reserve early. In
December
, the Kamundagan Christmas festival lights up downtown.

Hotels cluster around downtown (Centro), where the cathedral and Plaza Quezon are, along Magsaysay Avenue, and near the malls. In-town inns and budget hotels run about
a night, mid-range hotels with pools and restaurants run about
, and the city's best hotels run about
. Magsaysay Avenue, packed with cafes, restaurants, and bars, is great for an evening walk, while Centro is convenient for touring the churches on foot.

Naga's signature dish is, without question, kinalas. Long-running kinalas shops line the riverside and downtown, each with its own slightly different sauce, and locals love it for breakfast. "Baka kinalas," made with beef, and broth with beef innards, are also popular. Bicol regional dishes like Bicol Express, laing, and pinangat are easy to find everywhere too.
Bigg's Diner, which started in Naga in

, has several branches around town, making it easy to grab a meal. Because it's a student city, prices overall are affordable, and cafe culture is well developed. Good souvenirs include pili nut snacks, hot chili sauce, and Bicolano pastries.
Kinalas is sold from early morning, and popular shops sometimes run out before lunch. It's best enjoyed as breakfast.
Avoid sleeveless tops and short shorts when entering the churches, and refrain from taking photos during Mass.
If visiting during the Peñafrancia Festival, book accommodation months ahead and check the procession schedule and road closures in advance.
Malabsay Falls can swell and turn murky the day after rain. It's best visited on a clear morning.
If you plan to go to Caramoan, stay a night in Naga and set out at dawn. In

there were reports that scheduled boats from Sabang Port to Guijalo don't run often because of rising fuel costs, so it's safer to check ahead whether boats are running, or take a bus or van that goes overland to Caramoan.
Bicol Central Terminal operates 24 hours, but if you arrive late at night, it's safer to take Grab or a taxi to your hotel.
ATMs are plentiful at downtown malls and banks, but jeepneys, tricycles, and small eateries accept cash only.
You can check festival schedules, traffic closures, and attraction information on the City of Naga tourism
official website

The Traslación and river procession of the Peñafrancia Festival draw enormous crowds, with risks of crush accidents and heat exhaustion. Children and the elderly should not get close to the procession and should watch from a safe spot.
Watch out for pickpockets during the festival and in downtown plazas in the evening, and keep valuables in front of you.
During the
August–November
typhoon season, low-lying areas along the Naga River can flood. Check weather advisories.
The rocks and steps at Malabsay Falls are slippery. Don't swim when the water is swollen.
Always wear a life vest and helmet when wakeboarding, and beginners should take a lesson first.
Agree on the tricycle charter fare clearly before setting off.
